title: Taco or Tostada Salad with Meat and Sour Cream

content.title: About
content.content: Taco or tostada salad with meat and sour cream is a Mexican-inspired dish that combines crunchy tostada shells or soft tortilla rounds, fresh vegetables, aromatic spices, sautéed meat (usually beef or chicken), and a generous dollop of sour cream. It can be served cold or slightly warm, often accompanied by guacamole, salsa, and a wedge of lime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A tostada is a fried corn tortilla that becomes a crisp base, popular in central Mexico.
Traditional taco meat is often grilled (asado) with chili, cumin, and oregano for a smoky flavor.
Sour cream adds a creamy tang, though some Mexican recipes use a lime‑infused crema instead.
The dish is commonly garnished with fresh cilantro, radish slices, and avocado.
Taco shells can be soft corn tortillas or fried to a crunchy texture.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides complete, high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and vegetables supply B6, B12, and niacin, supporting metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Sour cream contributes calcium and phosphorus, important for bone strength.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, bell peppers, and cilantro are rich in vitamin C and carotenoids that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fresh veggies and the tostada shell add fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces or salted tostadas can raise the sodium level, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Sour cream and fried tostadas add saturated fats; those monitoring cholesterol should moderate portions.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Some tortillas contain wheat; choose gluten‑free options if you have celiac disease.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Meat must be cooked thoroughly to avoid salmonella or campylobacter risks.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Lay out crisp tostada shells or split tortilla rounds, top with a mix of diced vegetables (tomatoes, cucumber, red onion), add seasoned sautéed meat, drizzle with sour cream, and garnish with cilantro, avocado slices, and lime wedges. Serve alongside guacamole and salsa.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tostadas separate to stay crunchy. Keep sour cream tightly sealed and use within its expiration date.
